title: Legacy protocol consolidation and client transition requirements
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Overview:
This ticket defines the product requirements, scope decisions, acceptance criteria, and rollout plan for consolidating legacy inference protocols (legacy streaming/polling endpoints and old model aliases) into the unified inference API. The goal is to provide deterministic client migration paths, explicit SLO/SLAs for transition windows, and clear SDK/console guidance to limit customer disruption.

Background:
Over the past three years we accumulated several endpoint families (legacy-stream, legacy-poll, chat-v1 aliases) to support backwards compatibility for early adopters. These paths complicate routing, increase maintenance burden, and prevent consistent observability and cost allocation. The engineering roadmap includes removing protocol-level special cases and standardizing on the unified generate/chat/stream routes with versioned model aliases.

Goals:
- Provide a low-friction client migration playbook that covers web SDKs, mobile SDKs, and server SDKs.
- Deliver console tooling to identify customers still using legacy protocols and offer one-click migration suggestions.
- Define a phased timeline and gating criteria that preserves production availability and provides fallbacks during rollback windows.
- Ensure all migration changes are covered by security review, audit logging, and telemetry.

Non-goals:
- This ticket does not include changes to model weights or model alias semantics (handled by model-onboarding PRs).
- We will not remove protocol handlers until after at least two customer-facing cycles of communications and automatic migration attempts.

Scope - In:
- Product requirements and PRD for migration flows.
- Acceptance criteria for console-migration reports, SDK compatibility shims, and telemetry dashboards.
- Customer-facing docs, migration CLI script, and email templates.

Scope - Out:
- Rewriting of third-party SDKs (we will provide adapters and guidance only).
- Backend kernel/runtime changes unrelated to routing or telemetry.

Functional requirements:
- Console: Add a per-customer usage table that shows last 90-day calls per endpoint family and highlights legacy protocol usage.
- API: Ensure unified generate endpoints accept both legacy payload shapes and canonical payloads for a 6-week compatibility window (compat-shim).
- SDKs: Add opt-in compatibility flag (compatMode: true) that users can set to automatically translate legacy client calls. This flag must default to false for new SDK releases but be enabled via console for targeted customers.
- Rollout gating: Automated canary that detects increased 5xxs or latency and automatically pauses migration for affected customers.
- Telemetry: Tag all translated requests with migration_variant=compat-shim and emit metrics for translation ratio and translation failure reasons.
acceptance_criteria: Console shows legacy endpoint usage for 95% of customers with >7 legacy calls/day within 48 hours of rollout.
SDK adapters correctly translate 99.9% of common legacy payload shapes in synthetic test suite (10k generated cases) with documented edge cases.
Automated canary rollout pauses within 15 minutes of a >3% absolute increase in 5xx rate compared to baseline and notifies on-call.
All translated requests are tagged and visible in the per-model telemetry dashboards within 1 hour of ingestion.
Customer support script and email templates validated by Support and Legal, and send successfully to a pilot group of 200 customers without bounce/backoff issues.
Security review signoff completed and audit log retention policy validated against compliance requirements.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (Pilot, weeks 0-3): Identify pilot cohort (200 customers) with console targeting. Enable SDK compatMode for cohort and monitor. Phase 1 (Gradual, weeks 4-8): Console recommends migration for customers that pass health checks. Enable automatic compat-shim at the API routing layer for recommended customers. Phase 2 (Aggressive, weeks 9-12): Start scheduled automatic translation for remaining customers with in-console opt-out and an extended notice window. Phase 3 (Retire, week 16+): After 8 weeks of full-translation coverage and no critical regressions, decommission legacy route handlers behind feature flag and provide final 30-day window before permanent removal.
communication_plan:
- Week -2: Publish PRD and migration FAQs to docs.redwood.ai.
- Week 0: Email pilot invite + console notification to pilot group.
- Week 4: Send migration readiness checklist and SDK upgrade notes to customers flagged as medium/high usage.
- Week 8: Public blog post and changelog update announcing consolidation timeline and deprecation dates.
- Ongoing: In-console banners for impacted customers with link to migration guide and one-click opt-out.
sdk_changes:
- Add compatMode boolean and translation library (JS/Go/Python) with stable API.
- Ship adapters with detailed changelog and automated test coverage.
- Provide migration snippets for common frameworks (Node Express, Flask, Rails) and sample code for handling streaming fallback.
- Deprecation Notice: New SDKs (from release console-2026.05) will default compatMode=false; customers can enable from console or via env var for server SDKs.
monitoring_and_alerting:
- Dashboards: Migration overview, translation-failure reasons, per-customer 5xx rate, latency P95/P99.
- Alerts: PagerDuty if translation_failure_rate > 0.5% for any customer with >1000 translated requests/day; alert if migration-related 5xx uplift > 1% over baseline across production.
- Postmortem: Any pause triggered by canary must result in a retro within 72 hours with action items and timeline adjustments.
risks_and_mitigations:
- Risk: Edge-case payloads produce incorrect generation outputs. Mitigation: Maintain a whitelist of known edge-case patterns surfaced by SDK and add explicit translation fallthrough to return 412 with migration guidance.
- Risk: Customers dependent on legacy streaming semantics for UI flows. Mitigation: Provide streaming shim and example UI migration patterns; extend pilot cohort to include high-risk customers.
- Risk: Increased operational cost due to double-writing telemetry during compatibility window. Mitigation: Cap translation at 10% of total traffic per customer during the Gradual phase and monitor costs weekly.
